name: goal-pursuit-monitor
description: Watch a goal that outside events move — check it, then PARK until a self-scheduled wake instead of burning cycles. Between checks the run costs nothing and survives gateway restarts; the next check is a clock trigger the run created for itself.

task.help: What you are monitoring and what outcome ends it. State the goal, not the polling mechanics — 'PR #123 is merged', 'the export job has finished', 'the vendor page announces the new API'.

check_instructions.help: How to perform ONE check — the commands to run, pages to read, or paths to inspect. Each cycle follows these instructions once.

success_criteria.help: When monitoring may END — the observable state that means the goal is met. Left blank, the monitor never self-completes and runs until you cancel it, which is the honest default for open-ended watching.

cadence.help: The default gap between checks, in plain language ('in 20 minutes', 'in 4 hours'). A check that sees change coming may schedule sooner; one that sees a dead calm may stretch it.

steering_examples.description: Watch PR #4521 until CI is green and it has an approval, checking every 30 minutes
Slow down — check twice a day instead, and only alert me on a red build

example_outputs: a goal watched to completion with checks logged and nothing burned between them

children.label: Parked until the self-scheduled trigger fires

config.message: This monitor is parked between checks. It wakes when its self-scheduled trigger fires (visible under Automations, created_by: agent, with an expiry). If it has been parked unusually long, the trigger may have expired or been deleted — answer this gate to force a check now, or cancel the run to stop monitoring.

children.label: One check, then schedule the next or finish
